title: the hollow-anchor fixture repo pins core.autocrlf false, so its worktree holds the bytes git stored on every box
intention: The _fixture in test_hollow_anchors_before_the_build_that_stands.py sets core.autocrlf false in its scratch repo right after git init, so the file the fixture wrote and the blob git holds are the same bytes and the anchor-holds-every-file tooth refuses as it does on Linux.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: on Windows test_an_anchor_holding_every_file_raises_naming_the_anchor returned a reading (verdict green, reasons empty, subject.py measured not unchanged) where it must raise; with core.autocrlf false in the fixture repo all 8 teeth of that proof are ok
traces_to: Law 3: measured, the worktree read CRLF and the blob LF under autocrlf=true and the tooth went red to ok with the pin; Law 8: the proof reds on the unpinned fixture on any host.
how: One line after the git init in _fixture: _git(repo, 'config', 'core.autocrlf', 'false'). Red-first proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_anchor_fixture_pins_its_line_endings.py builds the fixture for real and reads the repo's own config, so it reds on Linux too.
